Re the reel of mullinavat.

The reel appears in Peter Cooper’s “The complete Irish fiddler”. It caught my attention because my grandparents are buried there. My grandfather Pat Wallace had a good reputation as a fiddler around the area and hailed from nearby Ballyquin. I don’t know if he ever played this reel. I have had a go at it but have never seemed to commit it to memory.

↳ Posted by the mullinavat fiddler on May 19th, 2008.

Andy McGann’s Setting of The Reel of Mullinavat

This is how Andy McGann played this one.
I’ve never heard two people play this tune the same - so I just decided to stick to this setting. That c natural in the second go around of the a part is what sold me.

The Reel of Mullanavat

Re: The Reel Of Mullinavat

Not only top-class fiddle playing in this clip, but excellent piano accompaniment - though unfortunately the player isn’t credited here. Underlines the point made very often in these pages that, to do it well, a backing musician needs to really know the tunes.

↳ Posted by Bazza on February 15th, 2021.

Re: The Reel Of Mullinavat

The accompanist was Deirdre McSherry from Co. Tipperary. She does indeed “know the tunes”, being one of the few players of Boehm-system flute I’ve come across who really makes it work.
Thank you for that comment, Bazza. I really should have given her credit in the caption, and that omission has been duly corrected.
